verses.text: The words of Amos, who was among the herdsmen of Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.
He said: “Yahweh  will roar from Zion, and utter his voice from Jerusalem; and the pastures of the shepherds will mourn, and the top of Carmel will wither.”
Yahweh says: “For three transgressions of Damascus, yes, for four, I will not turn away its punishment; because they have threshed Gilead with threshing instruments of iron;
but I will send a fire into the house of Hazael, and it will devour the palaces of Ben Hadad.

I will break the bar of Damascus, and cut off the inhabitant from the valley of Aven, and him who holds the scepter from the house of Eden; and the people of Syria shall go into captivity to Kir,”  says Yahweh.
Yahweh says: “For three transgressions of Gaza, yes, for four, I will not turn away its punishment; because they carried away captive the whole community, to deliver them up to Edom;
but I will send a fire on the wall of Gaza, and it will devour its palaces.
I will cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod, and him who holds the scepter from Ashkelon; and I will turn my hand against Ekron; and the remnant of the Philistines will perish,”  says the Lord  Yahweh.
Yahweh says: “For three transgressions of Tyre, yes, for four, I will not turn away its punishment; because they delivered up the whole community to Edom, and didn’t remember the brotherly covenant;
but I will send a fire on the wall of Tyre, and it will devour its palaces.”

Yahweh says: “For three transgressions of Edom, yes, for four, I will not turn away its punishment; because he pursued his brother with the sword, and cast off all pity, and his anger raged continually, and he kept his wrath forever;
but I will send a fire on Teman, and it will devour the palaces of Bozrah.”

Yahweh says: “For three transgressions of the children of Ammon, yes, for four, I will not turn away its punishment; because they have ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead, that they may enlarge their border.
But I will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah, and it will devour its palaces, with shouting in the day of battle, with a storm in the day of the whirlwind;
and their king will go into captivity, he and his princes together,”  says Yahweh.

footnotes.content: Amos the herdsman—just a working man from Tekoa—called to speak the Lord's words to a prosperous, comfortable Israel. How often does the Lord call the most unlikely vessels to say what no one wants to hear? There's comfort in that for those of us who feel small.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord's voice from Zion—not a whisper but a roar. When judgment comes wrapped in His word, even pastures mourn. I've learned that His silence can be scarier than His voice, and His voice, when it comes, means He has not abandoned us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Damascus crushed Gilead with iron threshing instruments—cruelty dressed up as conquest. The Lord sees not just the deed but the heart that delights in it. Notice that He counts the transgressions: three are bad, but four tip the scales. There is a limit to His patience, though His grace is long.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Fire consumes the houses of the mighty—Hazael and Ben Hadad's palaces. The Lord doesn't ignore the pride of nations. What makes us think our schemes escape His eye when kingdoms cannot?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The bar of Damascus broken, its rulers torn away, its people led captive to Kir. This is what happens when a nation builds itself on cruelty rather than justice. The Lord restores what the wicked destroy—not always here, but always there.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Gaza carried away whole communities to sell them to Edom—human trafficking, wrapped in commerce. The Lord sees the captive and the captor both. No cruelty is forgotten by Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Fire on Gaza's wall, devouring palaces. The image repeats: wherever injustice builds its house, the Lord's judgment finds it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ashdod, Ashkelon, Ekron—Philistine cities named and known. The Lord's hand turns against each. We live as if evil goes unnoticed; these verses remind us it does not.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Tyre's sin: delivering whole communities to Edom and forgetting the brotherly covenant. What a thing to forget—a bond of brotherhood. Many nations do this: break sacred trust for profit. The Lord remembers what they choose to forget.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Fire on Tyre's wall. Another palace falls. The pattern holds: those who choose betrayal over covenant reap what they sow.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Edom pursued his brother with the sword—a reference to Esau's ancient grudge against Jacob. Generation after generation, Edom nursed its anger, cast off pity, kept wrath forever. What a picture of hardened hatred: endless, without mercy. I've watched bitterness work like this, eating from the inside out.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Fire on Teman and the palaces of Bozrah. Even Edom's strongholds—places named for strength—cannot stand against the Lord's judgment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ammon ripped open pregnant women to enlarge their border. A sin so brutal it almost stops the breath. This is what happens when a people lose all reverence, when they measure worth only in land. The Lord abhors this.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Fire in Rabbah's wall, with shouting and storm—the Lord comes in judgment. Even in His wrath, there is an order, a day appointed, a clarity. He is not chaos; He is the Lord of all nations.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: King and princes go into captivity together. Readers today hear an echo in this: leaders who lead their people into injustice will go with them into judgment. The Lord still holds nations to account, though we forget it for seasons.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
